instruction.name: movfrh2gr.s
instruction.description: Extract the high 32 bits of fj into rd.

latencies.notes: 2 cycles for this direction. The split between the two directions is not observable on this core: every closed chain crosses the boundary both ways, so only the sum shows up (the round trip measures 5.00 cycles and stays additive). The split is fixed by the microarchitecture: an FPR load cannot take the address-bypass path, so `fld.d $f0, $r4, 0; movfr2gr.d $r4, $f0` (6.98 cycles) has to be a 5-cycle load plus a 2-cycle move, and the 5.00-cycle FPR round trip then puts the other direction at 3. The stored experiment is the round trip itself, with the opposite direction subtracted as chain_latency.
